# Instruments: Voice / choir

A note's `pitch` uses the **MIDI pitch (60 = middle C)**. Latest list: `muser instruments --family choir`.

| instrument | Recommended range | Polyphony | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `choir.aah` | 48–79 | 8 | Choir 'aah': open and bright; suited to chord beds |
| `choir.ooh` | 48–79 | 8 | Choir 'ooh': soft and dark |
| `choir.solo` | 48–79 | 2 | Solo voice (vowel) |

## Adjustable parameters (instrument_params)

Override the sound of the chosen instrument/preset; write only the items you want to change, the rest stay as they are. `muser instruments <name>` shows the preset's current values.

| Parameter | Range | Automation | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vowel` | 0 – 4, or `"a"` / `"e"` / `"i"` / `"o"` / `"u"` | ✓ | Vowel: "a" "e" "i" "o" "u", or a number 0-4 (e.g. 1.5 = between e and i). Good for automation |
| `attack` | 0.005 – 2 s | ✓ | Attack time |
| `release` | 0.01 – 4 s | ✓ | Fade-out time after release |
| `vibrato_rate` | 0 – 12 Hz | ✓ | Vibrato rate |
| `vibrato_depth` | 0 – 200 cent | ✓ | Vibrato depth (cents) |
| `brightness` | 500 – 12000 Hz | ✓ | Tone brightness |
| `breathiness` | 0 – 1 | ✓ | Breathiness |
| `singers` | 1 – 6 (integer) | — | Number of singers per note: 1 solo; 4-6 choir |
| `formant_shift` | 0.7 – 1.4 | ✓ | Formant scaling: <1 deeper, bigger voice; >1 thinner, smaller |

Automation column: ✓ = notes already sounding follow immediately; next note = affects only notes that start afterward; — = cannot be automated. See [automation.md](../automation.md).

Preset values of each instrument:

| instrument | `vowel` | `attack` | `release` | `vibrato_rate` | `vibrato_depth` | `brightness` | `breathiness` | `singers` | `formant_shift` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `choir.aah` | 0 | 0.18 | 0.35 | 5.2 | 22 | 4000 | 0.2 | 6 | 1 |
| `choir.ooh` | 4 | 0.18 | 0.35 | 5.2 | 22 | 2500 | 0.3 | 6 | 1 |
| `choir.solo` | 0 | 0.06 | 0.2 | 5.6 | 40 | 6000 | 0.12 | 1 | 1 |

### Tuning examples

- 'Ooh' vowel, 6 singers, on the dark side

  ```json
  { "instrument": "choir.aah", "instrument_params": {"vowel": "o", "singers": 6, "brightness": 2500} }
  ```


## Tips and common mistakes

- A choir suits long-chord pads (2-4 beats); short notes sound unnatural.
- `choir.solo` has polyphony 2 and suits only a single melody.
- **Humming lyrics**: write `"lyric": "la"` on a note, or add a `w:` lyric line in ABC that lines up with the notes in order (`w: yue liang sheng qi`; `hel-lo` is two syllables, `*` skips a note, `_` extends the previous syllable). Both pinyin and English spellings are accepted; tone numbers are ignored. **Vowels only**: each note sings the vowel of its syllable (a e i o u; pinyin e is sung as 'uh' and ü as i), diphthongs such as ai / ao / ia glide across within the note, and endings in -n / -ng close the mouth into a hum. Consonants are not sung (the 0.4 consonant simulation sounds like another voice, and is off by default), so what you hear is humming with changing vowels, not singing in which the words can be made out; for real sung words, export a MIDI with lyrics for singing-voice synthesis software, or have the user record a vocal. Lyrics are also written into the MIDI export (lyric events).
